reviews.text: I hope it remains like this, the most peaceful part of the Great Wall (not the most maintained though), visiting this is like having a me time on one of the 7 Wonders of the World, I was almost alone when I came here and it was on a Sunday. Was maybe a mixture of Luck and because I started my visit on the afternoon (got to enjoy the Sunset here), and instead of starting at the Main Entrance I started on the Exit, that ended my Trek at the Main Entrance, it was all worth it of what I paid the Taxi in getting there and going back to Peking, getting to enjoy it on my own seeing the Sunset, I was able to appreciate why is it called Jinshanling, translates the golden Mountain

Outside of Beijing, located at Hebei approximately two and half hour drive from Wangfujing Beijing. There are no crowds, no rush just great views and a cable car ride up, continuing with a relaxing climb up and down then back to the ticketing exit. Our driver and guide Leo from Beijing Walking is very friendly, knowledgeable, helpful and skilled in this area. Beautiful sights at the wall and beyond into the vast mountains to have a glimpse of what ancient civilisation experienced and the labour involved to build these particular section. An experience in Jingsanling is a must in comparison over the long queues and tourist modernisation at Mutianyu and Badaling section.

Jinshanling is THE best section of the Great Wall to visit. There weren’t more than 10 other people on the entire section, we just occasionally passed groups of 2 / couples. We visited on a Thursday and there was no wait. The chairlift was closed, but we took the shuttle up to the west side, hiked across to the easternmost tower, and hiked down the past to the east entrance. Couldn’t be happier to see the wild, original, and unrestored wall. Beyond stunning and you just have to see it in person!

I stay at a farmhouse near the office entrace so I got there early. I can pay for ticket at the entrance by WeChat. There were not crowded in the morning. I walked along the Great Wall....Million of beautiful !!! Some sections were steep but I can hold the wooden ladder and climb up. Exhausted but happy. 😍

We booked our trip on Trip.com and it turned out perfectly! Our guide was Susie and she and our drivers were spot on. We had to transfer to a van the last 30 minutes of the trip. This section of the wall is not as popular as the others due to the distance from Beijing, it was a 4 hour round trip. The payoff is very few people, the views and original parts of the wall. After spending the previous day walking around the Forbidden City and my old knees we opted to ride the cable car up and take a casual walk/climb to the East Gate, took a bit over 2 hours.

Wow! Even with all the hype this experience was incredibly underrated! The wall itself is breathtaking. Jinshanling section is well maintained and very beautiful. We lucked out on crowds as often felt like we were the only ones up there. Town had some decent little restaurants and plenty of small vendors eager for customers (sometimes aggressively so). But still a pleasant community and area to visit. Stayed only one night and were able to see the wall as far as was open to the public in both directions. We're quite fit and that took us about 6 hours in total including lots of breaks to take pictures.
Trek from the east entrance to the west entrance took about 3 hours. Tickets cost 55 yuan per adult. This is the best section of the Great Wall of China we’ve visited so far. Like the General Tower .

In total awe. There's a direct bus from downtown beijing leaving at 8 am sharp on weekends. The trip takes 2,5h. Jinshanling is a less visited section as it's further out from beijing. So not so crowded as Mutianyu . Definitely try the farmhouse restaurant if you have an extra hour, amazing home cooked food for very reasonable prices and a very quaint, provincial Chinese feeling. Doesn't get more local than that. Visiting the great wall was one of the most amazing experiences of my life.

Historical and beautiful as it may be, I spent a lot of my visit focusing on my safety and dear life. Although I'm 57 and hiked 18,000 steps in Huangshan one day last year, this was a totally different kettle of fish. The unrestored parts had little or no parapets and the floor at places was so steep that I slipped once and found it hard to stop myself. The guide suggested that we get off the wall at one point to walk on the narrow and rocky dirt trail outside between 3 or 4 towers but that was even worse as a sudden slip or fall down the mountains could have injured us badly or worse. Furthermore, we hiked up and started from the east gate, walked down from the central section and didn't take the cable car up or down. Younger and fitter people may find it easier but be warned that it's not a stroll in the park. Perhaps the Mutianyu section would have suited me better. Rather cloudy that evening, so there wasn't a spectacular sunset.

The most beautiful point of the great wall in my opinion, why? Because it’s not full of tourists, so it’s not crowded and if you go there during the afternoon it’s empty. It’s juts you and the great wall with amazing views 🥰

Super nice section of the wall. I’ll list the specifics here, as I’m convinced the wall itself doesn’t need any explaining. You can take the train from Beijing every morning and evening (two trains a day). In high season it’s smart to book tickets in advance (can do so through Trip) We paid 69-70¥ for a taxi to drive us to the entrance. You don’t need a passport to buy tickets at the office (you do need it for the train). I forgot how much tickets are for the wall. There’s shuttles to the “start” of the wall, but the walk is only a km or so. You be the judge (we walked). You can head to the three starting points of the wall, west gate, central tower or east gate. If you start from the west gate, you can walk all the way through to the east gate. The climbs on the wall itself will be heavier. If you choose the east gate, the climb there is heavier but walking on the wall is lighter. It requires a shuttle or cab to go there though. (I think 40¥). If you pick the central gate, that’s what most tourists do, it traverse the most restored part of the wall. Doesn’t take up much time. For avid hikers it’s a half day trek west to east. For slow photography just a bit more. Going up and down from BJ is losing some time travelling and arriving around noon, but you still have time to see everything before turning back. This section of the wall really is beautiful, calmer than most and offers exceptional views.

This place is really under-rated and suggest you to come if you are hesitating. It’s authentic and real, it’s a bit far from central Beijing but definitely worth the time to be here. There is almost no tourist! Suggest you to hire a private driver to bring you there and back which is the quickest way. You don’t need to buy ticket in advance because no one comes there! Make sure you bring water and food. And use sun cream! There are two routes , one is to west and one is to east. The pictures I posted here is the route to east , which means you enter from the middle gate and get out from the path on east gate. Not sure how the route towards west gate but definitely worth to check out both routes if you can give two days for this! I have to be back there one day! It’s connected to the Simatai Great Wall section but they blocked it! So if you want to continue towards east, you can also enter again from the Simatai tourist area.

Coming here was such an amazing experience! It was exactly what I had always imagined the Great Wall to be like! There were very few tourists and I came on a Saturday in summertime. I will say, if you are not in at least decent shape, this will be a very challenging section for you. The tours that come here will drop you off at one gate and pick up at the next one approximately 7km away. Wear hiking boots because there will be literally thousands of stairs between those two points. But if you can handle that, you won't regret coming here!

Jinshanling. Even the photographs, the documentaries, the whispered tales of its grandeur – none of it truly prepares you for the sheer, breathtaking reality of standing on this section of the Great Wall. You hear about its snaking path across mountains, its ancient stones whispering centuries of history, and its impressive scale. But to actually be there, feeling the cool stone beneath your fingertips, gazing at the seemingly endless serpentine form disappearing into the misty horizon – that's an experience that transcends mere description. What media often misses is the profound sense of connection to the past. You're not just looking at old stones; you're walking in the footsteps of countless laborers, soldiers, and travelers. The wind carries echoes of their efforts, their struggles, and their hopes. You can almost feel the weight of history pressing down, a tangible link to a civilization that built this monumental structure with sheer human will. And while the cable car at Jinshanling certainly makes access easier, don't mistake that for a diminished experience. The sensory feast is, in fact, heightened. The crisp mountain air fills your lungs with a freshness you rarely encounter in urban life. The panoramic vistas stretch out in every direction, a tapestry of rolling hills and verdant valleys that no screen can truly capture. The subtle variations in the stonework, the way the light plays across the ancient bricks, the quiet rustling of the wind through the surrounding vegetation – these are the details that truly bring Jinshanling to life, details that no photograph can fully convey. You can read about the watchtowers standing sentinel against the sky, but you can't grasp their strategic placement until you see the commanding views they offer. You can hear about the wall's resilience, but you can't truly appreciate the ingenuity of its construction until you examine the way the stones fit together, defying the elements for centuries. Jinshanling isn't just a historical site; it's a visceral experience. It's a reminder of human ambition, perseverance, and the enduring power of the natural world. It's a place that imprints itself not just on your mind, but on your senses, leaving you with a profound sense of awe that no amount of media consumption can ever replicate. You simply have to stand there, breathe it in, and let the majesty of Jinshanling wash over you.

The most beautiful part of the Great Wall of China, you find at Jin Shan Ling (金山岭长城风景区) walking over to Si Ma Tai Great Wall. Yes it is a longer drive from Beijing (2,5 hours) But without tourists around you can take raw pictures of the wall and feel the original and authentic Great Wall. I lived in China between 1998 and 2014 and we hiked several times and slept on this part of wall, knowing which tower to climb and sleep. We brought everything we would eat and drink, and left nothing behind. Plan it well. The walk is about 10km walk. The trail is steep and raw, but still in amazing condition. One time when we were getting ready to sleep, a Scorpion was crawling over the leg of one of the people coming with me, and I must say that the person did not sleep well after we killed it. Walk with care, bring enough water. Enjoy the Amazing Great Wall.

Jinshanling Great Wall is very picturesque. The hike is very challenging with some steep slopes, takes around 4 hours to complete it. Good fitness level is essential. The hike is very peaceful. This location of Great Wall is not very crowded, even during peak seasons.

Climbed the Jinshangling Great Wall during March and was pretty amazed by the views. The climb was fairly easy compared with Mutianyu and Simatai Great Wall. We stayed nearby at the Jinshangling Great Wall Hotel. There is cable car access to one of the sections of Jinshangling Great Wall. Either you can go up first or take it down after your climb.

5 stars? There’s not enough stars out there to rate this place! Way too good! Getting there was a bit of a hassle but it was all worth it. Definitely the best section of the wall. There were hardly any people, it was like we had the wall to ourselves. Definitely would recommend to all healthy individuals as there are some parts where it’s quite steep. Carry water and comfortable shoes.

Go to the end of the day! We went on a tour for the sunset, there were less than 10 people on the wall when we were walking around around. Highly recommend the two hour plus drive out to see this portion of the Great Wall.

We were contemplating which section of the Great Wall to visit and I’m glad that we visited Jinshanling. This section had both the old and the restored portions of the Great Wall and the climb was quite easy. It wasn’t crowded and we got a few areas of the Great Wall just to ourselves. We visited in the end of August and were blessed with lovely weather.

The Great Wall of China at its finest. The Great Wall of China, or as the Chinese call it the "Great Wall of 10,000 li" (万里长城: Wànlǐ Chángchéng), is one of the most iconic and imposing structures in the world (and no, you can't see it from space because it's too narrow). The history of the Wall, or rather the Walls, begins in the Spring and Autumn Period (722-481 BC), when various warlords built rammed earth defensive walls to protect their states. Qin Shi Huangdi, the first Chinese emperor, combined the northern walls in particular into one large stone defensive barrier. The Great Wall brought (partly) security, but also concerns, because maintaining and manning the wall was a costly affair that often led to the fall of a dynasty. The Great Wall as we know it today is the Ming Dynasty wall, stretching 6,300 km from Jiayu Guan in the west to Shanhaiguan and the Yalu River in the east. The Jinshanling sector is one of the most secluded sections of the Great Wall. Here, you can walk relatively undisturbed, take photos without crowds of other people, and enjoy the scenery and views in peace. The drive to Jinshanling is longer than to Badaling or Mutianyu, but it's absolutely worth it!

Absolutely stunning !!! booked a taxi from Beijing and left early morning around 5am and reached in 2.5hours. Visited During late December and there were no tourists. Thrilling views. Magnificent structure ! I was completely stunned to finally able to witness this incredible wall and especially in its most natural form..

Amazing quiet place in the month of March under a beautiful sky !!! Renovated and original part of the Great Wall in this area.. easy to travel there from Beijing and easy access at destination. For hiking lovers, for cable car lovers, all can enjoy in a quiet environment! A must!

To get here from beijing take the coach bus heading to Luanping from Wangjing West Subway Station and get off at the jinshanling great wall service area. Amazing uncrowded section of the wall where you can experience both restored and unrestored sections of the wall. Start from the east entrance and hike to the main entrance atop the wall or vice versa

It takes about 2.5hours to drive from central Beijing. This section has been renovated about 90% and it is being renovated further, so be quick! Also if you are visiting it in the next weeks/months, make sure it is still open, because they will be closing this section for renovations (which has already started!). When you get there you will be hassled by locals to buy beer, water, selfie sticks, etc... also some of them might help you with buying tickets or anything else, always expecting you to tip them. You won't need help really, signs are in English. You will buy the tickets for 65RMB each and if you want to take the cable car up to the wall (which I highly recommend) you will need to buy them once you are already inside for 40RMB. If you don't take the cable car you will need to go up a lot of stairs which will take you about 40 minutes! The cable car takes about 10-15 mins and saves you a lot of boring walk in the middle of nowhere up stairs with not very interesting views. The walk from the West to East section took me about 1.5hr. Some steep hills and stairs up and down, so bring some non-slippery shoes (I've walked with my Vans without a problem).

Started at the South Gate. Had a great hike of a couple of hours during the late Autumn season in mid November 2016 where the cable car service stopped, and we made the walk right up to the finishing point at the East Gate. It was very windy and the segment closer to Simitai was wild/unrepaired and simply love the way it was left untouched. There were very few tourists, this itself is a major plus point. The hike is moderate in difficulties as compared to Badaling and Mutianyu. If you are not a person who gives up easily, Its all worth the hike.

I was there in the middle of February, there was almost no tourists, but at the same time it was hard to get there by yourself. It is worth every cent u gonna spend to go there. Beautyful place, that You can feel the magic and history of the place!
Wonderful location with great views up to the Simatai section of the great wall. Both sections are diverse and worthwhile to see in a day trip. Jinshanling is particularly beautiful at sunset.

Suggest coming here to see the ‘real’ Great Wall as it is. There wasn’t a lot of tourists here and that was great. This is the wall in its natural state without being upgraded for tourism. Views are tremendous! Some of the steps are very steep here!
If you want a truly memorable Wall experience that transports you back in time, this is the section to visit. Definitely a long drive out here but for sure worth it.

Truly a jaw dropping portion of the Great Wall! Contains both restored and unrestored portion! Best of all this place is not as touristy as compared to more popular portions like Mutianyu, so there’s a lot of room for personal shots. It will require more effort to get there (I.e 2 hr journey from Beijing), but it is worth it.

One of the most beautiful parts of the Great Wall, this location is not crowded with tourists. The path to climb is quite hard and steep with stone steps, you need to prepare your health well and bring a few small bottles of water because there is no place to provide water on the way up the Great Wall. The road to the Great Wall passes through a peaceful, beautiful ancient town, this place you can visit to see the Great Wall lit up at night
Jinshaling is a little further away from Beijing but you get the Real Deal,... Original Structure, not renovated.

Our walk on the Jinshanling part of the Great Wall was absolutely breathtaking. We did a great many things during our trip to China, but the Wall hike at Jinshanling sticks as an unforgettable experience. We were picked up at our hotel and taken to Jinshanling by a car organised by (at)greatwallhiking(dot)com. It was a 2,5 hr drive during which our guide provided us with a lot of information on the history of the Great Wall. And because Jinshanling is a bit further away from Beijing than other Wall spots we were almost the only ones on the Wall - it was truly fantastic!

5 stars doesn't do this place justice. This part of the wall is not crowded at all (I could count the number of people I saw in late March) and is incredible. Has a lot of famous historical points as well. Bring comfortable shoes and water as this is a hike and many stairs. I highly recommend this part of the wall!

I visited the Great Wall way back in 1993, on my in my return to Hawaii. It has a very long history all the back in the 1300, the only man made visible in the moon, hundred of thousand people perish during the construction of that magnificent icons, it's was constructed to prevent the Mongols & Turks from entering the city.

Amazing. So worth the extra to get here. Even then only two hours from Beijing. Don’t let anyone put off coming just because it’s in a different province which means road blocks and checks. In the whole time there were less than 50other people there all day. In places the wall was restored but the best bits were to the East where it soon becomes authentic. Really fabulous.

A really beautiful area. Even without the wall it's still a gorgeous trip to the mountains, and climbing the wall was amazing. Not too crowded. This is not recommended for those who are not very mobile. Those who have difficulty with stairs are advised against attempting this section.

It is on the border between Beijing and Hebei province and on the way to Mountain Resort of Chengde or Bishu Shanzhuang. It is one of the best kept Great Wall secrets. Since it is far away from Beijing (2+ hrs drive), there are relatively few people. Plus, the area has the combination of old wall, half refurbished wall, and some new walls. You can find every type. The hike can be long or short. But it is pretty easy in general. The best part is that you can be away from Beijing's smog. Been there some 30 yrs ago. It has changed a lot since then. Gate tickets are a bit pricey. Be prepared. There is no directions. Maps are not very well marked. Easy for kids. Or you can try the gondola. The entrance fee is a bit pricy.
Less crowded than the other parts of the Great Wall but quite a distance away. Best to go with a tour agency especially if you are unable to speak Mandarin

This section probably has less traffic than the others but that's what makes it better. No crowding or jostling, nice peaceful and quiet walks, no hawkers. Just beautiful scenery in a magnificent setting.

The Great Wall at Jinshanling is about 155 kilometers away from downtown Beijing and stretches from Miyun County of Beijing to Luanping County of Hebei Province. It is the best preserved part of the Great Wall in the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) with many original features. Jinshanling connects to the Great Wall at Simatai in the east and Great Wall at Gubeikou in the west. The name of Jinshanling comes from two watchtowers, Great Jinshan Tower and Small Jinshan Tower on the Great Wall in this region. It was said that 3,000 soldiers from Jiangsu and Zhejiang provinces, under the command of famous Ming General Qijiguang (1528-1587), built two watchtowers and named them after the Great Jinshan Island and Small Jinshan Island in their hometown to show their sentimental feelings.
This the best Great Wall I ever climbed. Not crowded n a mix of semi restored great wall and the original.
The most beautiful place to walk in the Great Wall. My husband and I were totally by ourself and we took amazing photos.
Great Wall, Great views. Excellent place to take pictures. There was not so many people on the evening, you can take Great photos.
It is definitely a great place, not only because of its scenery, but also the memory I shared with my family when I left from Beijing to North America.
Far away from Beijing. 2:30h without traffic jam, but really nice and less tourists. Perfect place...
For me the best part of the wall you can visit. It is far away from Beijing, but totally worth it.
Spectaticular and original view of great wall.......promminent look and real taste of greatness , really worth the visit.

Scegliere quale tratto di Muraglia visitare non è facile. Noi abbiamo scelto Jinshanling perché, essendo tra le sezioni meno comode da raggiungere, è solitamente poco affollata. In effetti ce la siamo goduta alla grande, praticamente deserta. Tanti si affidano ad un Didi, per godere di maggiore libertà, però i costi sono alti perché parliamo di 2 ore e 15 minuti di strada sola andata. E a questo tempo va aggiunta l’attesa per il ritorno e il ritorno stesso. Noi ci siamo affidati ad un piccolo tour organizzato. 40 euro ben spesi su un pullmino da 12 persone, quindi, tutto sommato, una cosa intima. Ci hanno portati all’entrata est, spiegandoci l’itinerario da seguire per arrivare al traguardo, cioè l’entrata ovest. 6 km, che sembravano pochi, ma sono stati piuttosto faticosi. Primo per il caldo, secondo perché tra una torretta e l’altra si scende e si sale…e ogni tanto nemmeno una volta sola. Inoltre a Jinshanling c’è un tratto restaurato e un tratto autentico, che quindi richiede una fatica tripla a causa del dislivello, dei gradini assenti e del fondo sconnesso. Siamo stati abbagliati dalla bellezza della Muraglia. Davvero ripaga sforzi, fatiche, soldi…tutto quello che volete.

Toch echt wel een wereldwonder! Mega mooi wandelgebied met fenomenaal uitzicht en genoeg historie om in te verdiepen. Niet de steile trappen onderschatten als je daar met je grote schoenmaat over moet klimmen, vooral als het regent.

Von Beijing fährt man circa 2 Stunden zu diesem wunderbaren Ort, wo man dieses beeindruckende Baudenkmal in seiner großartigen Naturlandschaft erleben kann. Dieser Ort ist wenig besucht und man kann sehr ungestört auf der großen Mauer viele Kilometer entlang laufen. Fit sollte man dazu jedoch unbedingt sein, denn es geht immer hoch und runter und es sind viele Stufen zu bewältigen, die touristische Versorgung ist überall gegeben und es ist unglaublich beeindruckend, was hier geschaffen wurde und bis heute sehr respektabel erhalten wird. 我爱中国🇨🇳

Quasiment seul sur la muraille en plein mois d'été (29 juillet 2024). Cette portion de muraille est plus éloignée de Pékin, mais elle vaut vraiment le coup de se rajouter un peu de temps de route (2h30 de trajet en taxi au total). Possibilité d'acheter les billets sur place (pas de file d'attente). On accède à la muraille via un télécabine. La zone est très sauvage, vallonné et végétalisée. Nous avons pu faire un grand tour sur la muraille de 3h de marche (il est possible de faire moins ou plus). Ce qui est super c'est qu'une portion de la muraille a été rénové alors qu'une autre est encore en ruines. Cela permet de voir l'impact du temps sur la muraille et le travail réalisé. Enfin, le prix pour 2 personnes étaient (en été 2024) de 210 CNY (26€) l'entrée et 1030 CNY (130€) de taxi A/R. Soit 78€ par personne. Nous ne regrettons absolument pas d'avoir payé ce prix car l'endroit est magique, il n'y avait personne et c'est l'un de nos plus beaux moments en Chine.
休日でも混んでいない万里の長城。 少し奥まで歩くと修復されていない区域になり、とても雰囲気が良い。ひたすら歩くが売店や行商のおばちゃんもしっかり存在するので水分補給も安心。 さらに良いポイントでショートカットの下山ルートまであるので帰りに来た道を戻らずに済むので嬉しい。 交通は不便なのでタクシーやマイクロバスをチャーターするのが楽だろう。
Genau der richtige Ort, um die große Mauer mit wenig anderen Leuten betrachten zu können. Wir waren überrascht, wie viele Fotos wir ohne andere Menschen machen konnten. 😍👍

北京近郊的金山嶺長城是我個人推薦要去長城當好漢的首選,八達嶺和居庸關雖然知名,但盛名之累,人多是不管什麼季節和時段的常態,想要一覽長城之美又不想太多人工修築痕跡,也不想到此一遊的遺憾,金山嶺野長城是第一選擇,這兒不僅是也好遠眺綿延長城,還可以體驗未加太多人工修整的坍塌長城,也可以挑戰自己的膽子和腿力,尤其夕陽時刻,整個金山嶺如其名,在夕陽的印托下,金光閃閃,美不剩收...最重要的是遊人不是很多,適合自駕游的行程安排,建議秋天季節最是美麗,可以安排去承德路上就可以半途一覽.附近還有個司馬台長城近年來也是熱門野長城首選,不過這幾年的人工休憩建築整理後,也是遊人眾多..還不如這個名氣較低,但景色第一的金山嶺長城來的私房景點

Magique ! Perchée dans les montagnes, la grande muraille serpente entre les sommets, offrant un paysage à couper le souffle entre histoire et nature. Le site est accessible à pied après une petite randonnée (inutile de prendre les télécabines ou les navettes) et il n'y avait pas trop de monde. Avec un grand soleil et le redoux du printemps c'était parfait

La muralla China para ti. Zonas son reconstruir junto a otras renovadas. Es una auténtica pasada de sitio. No es fácil llegar y tienes que cuadrar los tiempos con los autobuses, porque son hasta las 4.30 pm, que no te pille el toro porque luego el taxi a Pekín sale por un ojo de la cara, que lo sepas.
Nada masificado en temporada baja, eso sí un frío de la leche! Trayectos complicados en algunas zonas y muchos escalones rotos. Zona auténtica y sin a penas restauración con increíbles vistas.
Increíble lugar para hacer un trekking con muy poca gente De la puerta Este a la Oeste hay 12 kms espectaculares
Bellissima location, lontana dal traffico turistico, a circa un paio di ore da Pechino, ristrutturata solo in parte, molto realistica e assolutamente incredibile

Die aller beste Entscheidung hierher zu kommen. Es war bereits mein dritter Besuch an der chinesischen Mauer, u.a am Einstieg Badaling. Für die perfekte Mauer-Experience: Privates Taxi aus Beijing nehmen (Kosten bei uns 800 Yen + Mautgebühren) und früh morgens losfahren (wir sind um 5 Uhr losgefahren und haben im Auto gefrühstückt). Sehr sehr wenige Touristen, man hat größtenteils große Mauerabschnitte komplett für sich. Immer wieder kommt man an Ständen mit Wasser und Eis vorbei. Wirklich sehr entspannt, kein Gedrängel, schöne und saubere Mauerabschnitte, ein Traum 👍👍👍 Tickets Vorort kaufen, ohne Vorreservierung am Schalter, 65 Yen pro Person 👍

Super schöner Abschnitt der Großen Mauer. Gut erschlossen, schönes Wandergebiet. Gelegen etwa 120 km nordöstlich von Peking, erreichbar über eine Autobahn. Auch nie wirklich leer, aber deutlich ruhiger als Badaling.

reviews.authorName: TIME MACHINE LA MAQUINA DEL TIEMPO #TMMDT
reviews.text: Uno de los tramos mejor conservados de la muralla china. Próxima a beijing a dos horas y un lugar espectacular para caminar. No dejes de visitarla toda la aventura en Youtube así #tmmdt
Expérience hallucinante!! Il n'y a pas beaucoup de monde. Les points de vues sont à couper le souffle! Un voyage dans le temps. Un souvenir pour la vie. 🌎🌸👍
Weit weg von Peking, dafür hat es hier sozusagen keine Leute. Die Mauer ist hier echt genial und super lange!
Had a wonderful experience.
Fun hike. Cam be steep for some folks.
The Great Wall is even greater than we expected!
One of the best place I've ever seen in my life. Period.
Fab, dodgy steps though
